## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 75 (*Udakeuccāra*, "Defecating in water") is the final training rule (*sekhiya*) governing monastic etiquette in the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule regulates personal decorum and environmental cleanliness, prohibiting monastics from defecating, urinating, or spitting into water unless they are sick [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the rule and its accompanying case material is provided on SuttaCentral by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this training rule is preserved across virtually all surviving Vinaya lineages [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali tradition, it corresponds directly to Bhikkhu Parivāra Sekhiya 75, the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha, and the parallel code for nuns in the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (Bi-Vb Sk75), Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha, and Bhikkhunī Parivāra [SuttaCentral]. Parallels in other early Buddhist schools include the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅgas and Prātimokṣas of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, and Dharmaguptaka traditions preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse data from DharmaNexus reflects extensive Pali-internal formulaic reuse, exhibiting substantial textual overlap with the *Bhikkhupātimokkhapāḷi-ṭīkā* (Tika Vin04t), the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (Bi-Vb Sk75), both Pātimokkhas, and standard introductory and framing passages in other Sekhiya, Pācittiya, and Khandhaka chapters [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments of the text with the Sanskrit *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* and the Tibetan version of the *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D4106-2) [DharmaNexus].
